**Stack position H7**, base `agent115/wear-split-6-retire-samsung` (#364 @ `1266038cd311f3dcfd8e472c04e3241a3061866b`). #362 is at 2,983 of its 3,000 ceiling, so this fix is a new piece (new-PR limit 1,500). Never merge alone: H1-H7 land as one.

**Size:** 1,270 changed lines (1,250 additions, 20 deletions); 179 production lines in 2 files, 1,091 test lines in 6 files. Under the 1,500 new-PR limit.

## What changes
- **Sol B-362-8 (was C-362-14).** `src/services/health/onDeviceState.ts`: every stored Connect grant now carries the phone's consent session (`wearables_on_device_session`, a random nonce with nothing personal, kept outside the `wearables_on_device:` prefix). In the state chain, sign-out enumerates keys, then **replaces the session before any removal**; when the new value cannot be written it removes the stored one. Then it removes the prefix keys as before. `getLocalAuthorization` honours a grant only when its session equals the stored one, so a grant that a failed `getAllKeys` or `removeMany` leaves on disk stays void in this run and after a restart. Fail closed: an absent or unreadable session, or a grant with no session, authorizes nothing. The next Connect starts a new session when none is stored; a session read failure on Connect rejects the grant write. `retireOnDeviceState()` with no source also removes the session (everything the module wrote). Feature not on main, so no stored grants predate the binding.
- **Sol B-362-9.** `src/services/authActions.ts`: `signOut` keeps its synchronous `stopOnDeviceHealthWork()` and the sign-out epoch bump, then runs the rest inside `try/finally { await healthStateRetired }` (it never rejects). The parallel clear no longer holds the health promise: its own `finally` awaits it, so a `clearUserCache`/`clearAllStorage` rejection never lets `logout` fire, or `signOut` settle, before the health drain. An earlier throw (for example identity drain) also settles only after it. Account deletion ends in the same `signOut()`.
- **C-362-13 remainder (Sol) = C-362-15 (Opus), same lines.** A failed grant write restores the latest grant that reached disk (`authCommittedAt`), never another failed reservation.
- **Sol B-369-1 (fix round 1; the B-362-8 remainder, was builder C-369-1).** `src/services/health/onDeviceState.ts`: every grant is also bound to a consent authority in **SecureStore** (`wearables_on_device_authority`, Keychain / Keystore, a random nonce), a different store from the AsyncStorage backing store that holds the grant, the session and the progress. `retireOnDeviceStateAtSignOut()` revokes the authority **at once** (before the chain waits for any native AsyncStorage operation in flight) and **again first thing in the chain** (a grant write in flight may have started a new one), before any AsyncStorage write; when the SecureStore delete fails it writes a new random value, which voids every grant as well. `getLocalAuthorization` honours a grant only when both its session and its authority match; an absent or unreadable authority, or a grant without one, authorizes nothing. It also returns null when a sign-out started while it was reading. Connect starts an authority when none is stored; a failed authority read or write rejects the grant write (no unbound grant). `retireOnDeviceState()` with no source revokes the authority too. So an outage of every AsyncStorage mutation at sign-out, or an app exit while sign-out waits behind a held native write, no longer revives the old grant after a restart. Same-session consent still survives a restart.
- **Sol B-369-2 (fix round 2).** `src/services/health/onDeviceState.ts`: a Connect grant write already running when sign-out starts used to go on after the immediate authority revocation, create a new authority (or use a session read before sign-out) and bind a grant to it, so an app exit before the chain's second revocation kept consent. `serialWrite` now hands the write a `current()` check on the sign-out epoch; `recordLocalAuthorization` calls it after the session read, after a session write, after the authority read, after an authority creation, and with no await between the check and the grant write. Such a write rejects as stopped (`OnDeviceSessionChangedError`) and creates nothing; the chain still waits for its native step and revokes the authority again.

## Tests (in this piece)
- `src/services/__tests__/authActions.storageOutage.sol119g.test.ts`: Sol's H7 probe, byte-identical; it is Sol's H46F suite (`authActions.restartGrant.sol119f`, which it replaces) plus the AsyncStorage mutation-outage case, a pure addition.
- `src/services/health/__tests__/onDeviceState.failedGrantChain.sol119f.test.ts`: Sol's narrow C-362-13 remainder suite, byte-identical.
- `src/services/health/__tests__/onDeviceState.signOutDurable.test.ts` (10 cases): getAllKeys and removeMany failure plus restart; session write and removal both failing; a grant write in flight at a failed sign-out; persistence-positive and successful-clear controls; new Connect after a failed sign-out (now and after restart); unreadable or missing session and session-less grants fail closed; a session read failure on Connect.
- `src/services/__tests__/authActions.healthDrainFinally.test.ts` (3 cases): rejection inside the parallel clear, rejection before it, no-rejection control; held native write, logout ordering.
- `src/services/health/__tests__/onDeviceState.authorityStore.test.ts` (10 cases, fix rounds 1 and 2): every AsyncStorage mutation failing at sign-out plus restart; an app exit while sign-out waits behind a held native write; B-369-2: a Connect write held at its session read or at its authority creation when sign-out starts, restart taken while the chain's second revocation is held; a failed SecureStore delete; unreadable, missing and authority-less grants fail closed; an authority write failure on Connect; a sign-out during a grant read; same-consent restart and full-retirement control.

- `src/services/health/__tests__/onDeviceState.signOutDrain.test.ts` (fix round 2, one case updated): a grant write in flight at sign-out now rejects as stopped; the sweep still waits for it and no key or grant is left.

## Residual (documented, not claimed fixed)
The AsyncStorage-only residual of the opening (B-369-1) is closed. An old grant can now come back after a restart only if, in the same sign-out, SecureStore rejects both the authority delete and the replacement write AND AsyncStorage rejects the session write, the session removal and the prefix removal: two separate OS stores failing together. In that case the token deletion in the same SecureStore has failed as well (see the follow-up on `secureStorage.removeItem` in the B-HC9-119 report).
